newsitem.title: CANADA: Noranda sees higher prices in 1997-98.
newsitem.headline: Noranda sees higher prices in 1997-98.

text.p: Noranda Inc said on Thursday that demand for its products remained strong and that prices should gradually rise over the balance of 1997 and into 1998.
"Looking ahead, we are optimistic that 1997 can be a good year for Noranda for a number of reasons," Noranda Chief Executive David Kerr said in a statement.
Noranda posted net income of C$59 million in the first quarter of 1997, compared to C$36 million in the fourth quarter of 1996 and C$101 million in first quarter of 1996.
Prices for zinc, aluminum, copper, nickel and natural gas improved in the first quarter from the fourth quarter of 1996.
Strong results from Noranda's oil and gas operations also offset weaker markets for most forestry products, Kerr said.

Looking ahead, Kerr said that "consumption levels for most of our commodities remain strong and prices for most of our commodities are expected to gradually increase over the balance of the year, and into 1998."
Noranda's stock was unchanged at 30.30 in turnover of 188,000 shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
